description: Python code. Respect the project's supported versions and configured tooling.

rules.title: Use consistent Python conventions
rules.guidance: MUST follow configured Python formatting, naming and import conventions. Avoid unrelated style churn and do not require newer syntax than the supported runtime.

rules.title: Type meaningful boundaries
rules.guidance: SHOULD annotate public and complex boundaries with meaningful types. Run the adopted type checker; remember that annotations do not validate untrusted data at runtime.
rules.rationale: Clarify contracts without false validation claims.
verification: Type checker and boundary validation tests

rules.title: Avoid shared mutable defaults
rules.guidance: MUST do not use mutable objects as function defaults unless shared state is deliberate and documented. Create per-call containers inside the function where needed.

rules.title: Close resources reliably
rules.guidance: MUST use context managers or explicit try/finally ownership for files, connections and other closeable resources. Cleanup must also occur on failure.

rules.title: Catch errors deliberately
rules.guidance: MUST catch specific exceptions when recovery is meaningful. Broad catches belong at explicit containment boundaries; preserve failure information and never silently pass.

rules.title: Preserve async cancellation
rules.guidance: MUST when using asyncio, avoid blocking the event loop with synchronous IO or CPU work. Await owned tasks, bound concurrency and preserve cancellation after cleanup.
rules.rationale: Keep asynchronous work responsive and bounded.

rules.title: Invoke subprocesses safely
rules.guidance: MUST pass subprocess arguments as separate values where practical. Do not interpolate untrusted text into shell commands; set timeouts and inspect return codes when commands affect correctness.
